purpose: Claims-controlled external evidence register for defensive quantum-cryptography migration analysis.
claims_boundary: External publications, measured demonstrations, vendor roadmaps, prototype/manufacturing evidence, and proposed decoder architectures support the scientific and planning premises listed here. They do not constitute external validation of Worldshepherd, proof of a production key break, or proof that a cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists today.

items.finding: Complete secp256k1 ECDLP circuits are reported at <=1200 logical qubits and <=90M Toffoli gates or <=1450 logical qubits and <=70M Toffoli gates; stated superconducting scenarios execute in minutes with fewer than 500,000 physical qubits under the paper's assumptions.
items.allowed_use: External benchmark and migration-risk input only.

items.finding: A trapped-ion Walking Cat architecture estimate reports 1,457 logical qubits, about 39M Toffoli gates, 19,397 physical qubits and 25.7 days per secp256k1 ECDLP attempt under the paper's assumptions.
items.allowed_use: Architecture-specific sensitivity bound; not a demonstrated cryptographic break.

items.finding: IonQ's public roadmap targets 10,000 physical / 800 logical qubits in 2027 and 20,000 physical / 1,600 logical qubits in 2028. The 2028 target numerically overlaps IonQ's own published Walking Cat secp256k1 attack envelope.
items.allowed_use: Forward migration-planning trigger only; never Q-day or demonstrated capability.

items.finding: IonQ reports fully integrated 256-qubit Superion QPUs fabricated at SkyWater, first ions trapped in prototype systems, orders open, customer deliveries planned for 2027, and prior breakeven qLDPC QEC on a Tempo engineering system as validation of key Walking Cat elements.
items.allowed_use: Roadmap-maturity evidence. It raises confidence that the platform is progressing beyond slideware but remains far below the 20,000-qubit attack-scale target.

items.finding: A trapped-ion experiment demonstrates multiple QEC codes including a qLDPC code encoding four logical qubits in 18 physical qubits, with reported breakeven behavior in some instances.
items.allowed_use: Component-level QEC maturity evidence only; not an attack-scale overhead estimate or proof that the full Walking Cat cryptanalytic stack has been built.

items.finding: The paper proposes generalized qLDPC predecoding that processes over 90% of the decoding workload, reports up to 3,963x decoder-utilization reduction, and gives hardware designs sized for about 1,200 bivariate-bicycle logical qubits on one FPGA or 36,000-360,000 on a cryogenic ASIC.
items.allowed_use: Classical-decoding bottleneck sensitivity input only. Exact Walking Cat code compatibility, physical implementation at stated capacity, and attack-specific integration are unproven.

items.finding: A complete prime-field ECDLP Shor construction is reported at 835 logical qubits for a 256-bit curve, with a large Toffoli cost whose leading term is 919*n^3/log2(n).
items.allowed_use: Logical-width frontier only; no physical runtime may be inferred without architecture-specific compilation.

items.finding: The [[20,2,6]] C4-Helix architecture was experimentally validated on Quantinuum Helios, including repeated QEC, logical Clifford benchmarking and heterogeneous-code logical entanglement, with encoded results outperforming physical baselines without postselection.
items.allowed_use: Independent trapped-ion hardware-QEC progress input only; no cross-vendor resource multiplication.

items.finding: A trapped-ion experiment demonstrates a fault-tolerant universal logical toolbox and a small encoded Grover search on logical qubits.
items.allowed_use: Independent technology-trend evidence that non-Clifford/universal logical operations are hardware-demonstrated at small scale; not evidence of attack-scale integration.

items.finding: QCRYPTO migration-risk controls are under draft review in PR #208. Exact-head CI evidence must be refreshed after each convergence-model update before any readiness claim is promoted.
items.allowed_use: Internal software-quality evidence only; not independent scientific validation or external certification.
